purpose: Curated methodology corpus distilled from all thirteen user-supplied forensic reports. It teaches evidence selection, query planning, deduplication, coverage checks, Objective/Procedure/Observation structure, Annexure traceability and cross-source synthesis. Example case values are never current-case facts.

sources.name: Azim Lalani Google Takeout Forensic Report.pdf

training_rules: Reference reports teach methodology and wording, never current-case names, counts, dates, URLs, device identifiers or conclusions.
Section B artifact totals are candidate evidence inventory. A broad artifact count is not automatically the answer to a Section C objective.
Section C must resolve Objective -> Procedure -> relevant artifact families -> record-level evidence -> exclusions -> deduplication/correlation -> finding -> limitation -> plain-language meaning.
Section D Annexure is the traceability layer. A positive Section C observation should be reproducible from specific Annexure/source records where a suitable Annexure exists.
Section E Analysis Summary must restate the final Section C conclusion and must not independently invent or contradict a finding.

Presence is different from use; access is different from transfer; installation is different from execution; connection is different from copying; a URL visit is different from download/upload; a cleanup tool being installed is different from proof that it erased evidence.
When an expected artifact family is unavailable or incompletely collected, return INCONCLUSIVE rather than NOT_FOUND.
Platform-specific evidence must be respected. A Windows-only artifact cannot be treated as absent on Linux merely because no Windows record exists.

Raw technical rows must be classified before narrative use. Interface, hub, camera, Bluetooth, internal-disk, resource/static-asset and integration/telemetry rows must not be promoted to a stronger finding without evidence supporting that interpretation.
A report may contain analyst inconsistencies. The current-case deterministic evidence and cross-section consistency rules override an inconsistent exemplar sentence.
Google Takeout/cloud-export reports require source/service coverage verification before interpreting Gmail, Drive, Activity, Calendar, Photos or permission records.
Email account identity must distinguish a currently configured/current account from historical correspondents, message participants and browser traces.
Shared-file metadata and permission metadata prove the sharing/permission state recorded by the provider; they do not by themselves prove that a recipient opened, downloaded or exfiltrated a file.
Master/cross-source summaries must reconcile duplicated evidence across disk, mobile and cloud sources and preserve the strongest source-specific provenance instead of adding raw counts together.

Derived counts such as distinct physical devices, distinct messages and distinct cloud files must be computed after source-specific semantic deduplication and must be reproducible from traceable records.

artifact_inventory.rule: Inventory counts are context; classify physical storage/mobile/remote-session records before Section C.
Use application identity and execution/session evidence separately.
Classify URL/service and preserve the distinction between service access and communication/content transfer.
Document type totals do not prove a file action, ownership or company relevance.
Message/item totals do not equal distinct email accounts.
Count supported protected objects; encryption/protection does not establish wrongdoing.
Media totals are inventory unless an objective asks for specific content.
Use these for correlation, execution/recent-use context and timestamps; do not substitute their total count for another objective.
Review browser history, cookies, cache and downloads at record level; a global web count is not a forensic finding.
Treat provider activity/device rows as service-specific records and deduplicate repeated export/telemetry entries before conclusions.
Count distinct messages/events/contacts using native identifiers where available; attachments and descriptions are linked content, not independent messages/events.
Separate file identity, sharing state, permission role and actual transfer/activity. Sharing or permission alone does not prove download/exfiltration.
Link album metadata to distinct media and deduplicate exported copies using provider IDs/hashes where available.

objective_patterns.canonical_title: Verify Use of Unauthorized Remote Access Tools
objective_patterns.client_objective: To determine whether remote access tools were present and whether the available evidence shows remote session activity.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Installed applications and relevant remote-session/system records were examined to identify remote access software and supported remote connectivity activity.
required_questions: Which remote-access applications are installed?
Is there execution evidence for those tools?
Are there RDP or other remote-session records?
Do the records prove unauthorized external control, or only presence/session traces?
decision_rules: Installed tool alone proves presence, not use.
RDP/session record proves a session trace, not that it was unauthorized.
Only call access unauthorized when case evidence separately supports that conclusion.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To determine whether USB storage, mobile devices or other relevant external devices were connected to the system.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Device-enumeration and connection records were examined and correlated to identify physical storage devices, mobile devices and relevant connection times.
required_questions: Which rows represent distinct physical external storage devices?
Which rows are hubs, interfaces, cameras, Bluetooth, input devices, internal disks or duplicate volumes?
Were mobile-device/Your Phone records present?
Is file transfer independently supported?
decision_rules: Deduplicate interface/volume rows to the physical device.
Exclude internal disks, hubs, cameras, Bluetooth and input devices from the external-storage count.
Connection does not prove file transfer.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To determine whether cloud storage services were accessed and whether the evidence supports any upload, download, sharing or synchronization activity.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: The browser history, internet activity, download records and available cloud-related records were examined to identify cloud services and any supported file-transfer or synchronization activity.
required_questions: Which distinct cloud providers have meaningful access records?
Are records top-level/history visits or only static resources, privacy pages, integration scripts or telemetry?
Is there evidence of upload, download, sharing or sync separate from access?
decision_rules: Name distinct supported providers.
Cloud URL access proves access only.
Do not claim upload/download/share/sync without a supporting transfer/sync artifact.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify use of web-based chat or communication platforms on the examined system.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Browser activity, messaging artifacts and relevant system records were examined to identify supported access to chat and communication services.
required_questions: Which communication services are supported by browser/app evidence?
Does evidence show platform access only, or message/call/file-transfer content?
Are static assets being mistaken for user activity?
decision_rules: Name supported services.
Service access alone does not prove messaging or file transfer.
Use message/attachment records for content-level conclusions.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify supported access to social media, entertainment and professional networking platforms from the examined system.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Browser history and related system records were reviewed to identify distinct social, entertainment and professional-networking services accessed from the system.
required_questions: Which distinct platforms have meaningful browser-history evidence?
Are rows direct page/navigation records or embedded icons/share/static resources?
Does the evidence prove only access or a specific user action/post/message?
decision_rules: Name supported platforms.
Do not infer posting, messaging or account ownership from a URL alone.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify relevant internet and network activity and determine whether the evidence supports communication, file sharing or data transfer to external sources.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Browsing records, network-related records, connection history and relevant file-sharing/communication evidence were examined and correlated.
required_questions: Which relevant external services/hosts were accessed?
What network/session records are present?
Is communication, file sharing or data transfer directly supported?
decision_rules: Access to a platform is a supported fact when record-level evidence exists.
Do not convert access into data-transfer or messaging without direct evidence.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To determine whether tools capable of cleaning, hiding, deleting or altering digital traces were present or used on the system.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Installed applications, execution evidence and relevant system records were examined for cleanup, wiping or trace-hiding utilities and any supported evidence of their use.
required_questions: Which known cleanup/wiping tools are installed?
Is there execution/use evidence?
Is there evidence that the tool erased or concealed case-relevant data?
decision_rules: Presence proves availability only.
Execution requires execution evidence.
Erasure/concealment requires stronger activity evidence; do not infer it from installation.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To determine whether torrent-related services or artifacts were accessed and whether torrent-based downloading, uploading or file sharing is supported by evidence.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Browser records, download records, torrent/magnet artifacts and installed torrent-client evidence were reviewed for supported torrent-related activity.
required_questions: Are there true torrent/magnet/client artifacts or only unrelated URLs?
Was a torrent client installed/executed?
Is actual file transfer supported?
decision_rules: A torrent-related URL proves access only.
A .torrent/magnet/client artifact supports stronger torrent activity.
Do not claim download/upload/share without corresponding evidence.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To determine whether recovered URLs or related activity are associated with malware, phishing or other supported malicious indicators.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Recovered URLs, browser activity, downloads and available security-detection records were examined and correlated for supported malware or phishing indicators.
required_questions: Which URLs match a controlled malware/phishing classification?
Was the URL actually present in browser evidence?
Is there download, execution or security-detection evidence beyond URL access?
decision_rules: Report the URL access separately from infection/execution.
A suspicious or classified URL does not by itself prove compromise.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To verify the integrity and service coverage of the supplied Google Takeout export before interpreting account activity.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: The Takeout archive structure, hashes/manifests where available, and exported service folders were inventoried before service-specific records were parsed.
required_questions: Which Takeout archives/parts were supplied and hashed?
Which Google service folders and export files are present?
Are expected service sources missing, unreadable or encrypted?
Does the available export support a complete or only partial service-level examination?
decision_rules: Archive/service presence supports coverage, not completeness beyond the supplied export.
A missing service folder makes conclusions for that service inconclusive.
Never copy a reference report service count into the current case.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify Gmail communications relevant to the examination and distinguish messages, participants, attachments and account state.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Gmail MBOX/message records and related metadata were parsed; messages were deduplicated by native/message identifiers and correlated with attachments and participants.
required_questions: Which messages are sent, received, draft or other mailbox states?
Which addresses are current account identities versus historical correspondents?
Which attachments belong to which distinct message?
Are deleted/trash labels or historical records present, and what is their recovery state?
decision_rules: Count distinct messages, not attachment rows.
Correspondence with an address does not prove that address is currently configured on the account.
Preserve mailbox/label state and source message-id when available.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify files represented in the Google Drive export and the available metadata describing their paths, types and activity.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Drive file metadata and exported file records were inventoried, normalized and deduplicated using provider identifiers or stable path/revision attributes.
required_questions: Which distinct Drive files/folders are represented?
Which records show ownership, creation, modification or access versus only a local exported copy?
Are shared items separated from owned/My Drive items?
decision_rules: File presence in an export does not by itself prove a transfer event.
Use provider/native identifiers before file names for deduplication.

objective_patterns.canonical_title: Review of Google Account Activity Logs
objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify supported Google account activity events and the services/devices involved.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Exported activity records were normalized by service, timestamp and native event attributes, then deduplicated and correlated without treating telemetry rows as independent user actions.
required_questions: Which services have activity records?
Which events include usable timestamps/device context?
Are repeated telemetry/export rows duplicates of one activity?
decision_rules: An activity record supports the described event only to the level encoded by the source.
Do not infer intent from activity metadata.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify exported Google Calendar events and relevant event descriptions, participants, locations and timestamps.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Calendar export records were parsed and deduplicated by native event identifier or stable event fields; descriptions were treated as event content rather than separate events.
required_questions: How many distinct calendar events are present?
Which descriptions/participants/locations belong to each event?
Are recurring instances distinguished from duplicate export rows?
decision_rules: Do not count an event description as another event.
Preserve timezone and recurring-event identity where available.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify devices recorded by the Google account export and the available evidence of account access from those devices.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Device/account-activity records were normalized using stable device identifiers, model/platform labels and timestamps and were deduplicated before reporting.
required_questions: Which distinct devices are represented?
What stable identifier/model/platform supports each device identity?
Does the record show account access/activity or merely device registration?
decision_rules: Deduplicate repeated device rows to a stable device identity.
Registration/presence is not automatically proof of a specific user action.

objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify exported Google Photos media and album relationships relevant to the examination.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Photo/video files and Google Photos metadata were inventoried, linked by provider metadata or stable path/hash, and deduplicated before reporting.
required_questions: Which distinct media files are present?
Which albums/provider metadata reference them?
Are duplicate exported copies separated from distinct media?
decision_rules: Count distinct media by provider identity/hash where available.
Album membership is metadata context and must not duplicate the media count.

objective_patterns.canonical_title: Review of Google Drive Shared Files
objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify Drive items represented as shared and distinguish sharing metadata from file ownership or transfer.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Shared-item metadata and cloud-file records were correlated using provider file identifiers, owner/account fields and sharing state.
required_questions: Which distinct files/folders are marked shared?
Who is recorded as owner/sharer/recipient where available?
Does the source record sharing, access or an actual file transfer?
decision_rules: Shared status does not by itself prove download or exfiltration.
Do not infer ownership when only recipient/shared-with metadata is present.

objective_patterns.canonical_title: Review of Google Drive Shared Permissions
objective_patterns.client_objective: To identify permissions recorded for shared Google Drive items and the principals to which those permissions apply.
objective_patterns.client_procedure: Permission metadata was correlated to Drive items and principals, preserving role/type and source record identity and deduplicating repeated export entries.
required_questions: Which principals have permissions on which distinct files/folders?
What role/type is recorded (view/comment/edit/owner or equivalent)?
Are repeated permission rows duplicates of the same item-principal-role relationship?
decision_rules: A granted permission proves access rights, not that the recipient opened or transferred the file.
Report the role exactly as supported by the source metadata.

cross_section_consistency.description: A positive provider/device/platform/session finding should have at least one supporting record in the authoritative source set and, where selected, Annexure.
Section C cannot say no cloud/device/chat/social/RDP evidence when valid Annexure/source records establish the opposite.
Analysis Summary must reuse the finalized Section C finding rather than independently regenerate it.
Section B totals are not substituted for objective-specific distinct counts.
A zero/negative conclusion is permitted only when required evidence coverage is sufficient; otherwise use INCONCLUSIVE.

writing_style.source_basis: All thirteen supplied disk, data, Google Takeout/email and master forensic report exemplars were reviewed for recurring forensic-report methodology, evidence grammar and layout.
rules: Use formal, factual and concise forensic language; describe what was examined, what evidence was identified, and what the evidence does or does not establish.
Objective states the examination question in plain client language and does not contain a conclusion.
Procedure describes the forensic examination method and artifact families reviewed; it does not claim a result before the evidence is evaluated.
Observation answers the objective from current-case evidence, distinguishes presence/access/use/transfer, and states relevant limitations.
Prefer phrases such as The examination identified, The available records indicate, and No evidence confirming ... was identified when those statements are supported by current evidence.
Do not insert raw internal objective IDs, implementation terms, database field names, source code paths or unsupported technical noise into client narrative.
Keep the same finding consistent across Section C, Annexure and Analysis Summary.
Write each Objective, Procedure and Observation in full. Page packing is the Formation Agent's job; do not omit a finding to save space and do not invent filler to pad a page.
Write every Annexure table row in full. The Report Formation Agent packs leftover A4 body with the next URL rows; do not drop a row to save space and do not invent filler rows.
Never copy names, dates, counts, hashes, URLs, devices or conclusions from an exemplar into another case.

query_principles: Do not let an LLM execute arbitrary SQL. Resolve the objective to a controlled collector/report definition, then query versioned tables/views with bound parameters.
Filter by job_id/case id and tenant/schema at the first table access; never rely on a later in-memory filter for evidentiary isolation.

Use stable native identifiers for deduplication before timestamps/text. For devices prefer serial then VID/PID/model; for email prefer message-id; for cloud files prefer provider file-id/path plus revision when available.
Use equality/range predicates on indexed normalized columns for primary selection. ILIKE/regex/full-text are secondary discovery aids and must not replace an indexed case/job predicate.

Separate allocated/live, logically deleted, filesystem/trash recovered, WAL/journal/freelist residual and carved/unallocated states. Never merge an unverified residual candidate into a confirmed deleted count.
For zero-result conclusions record evidence coverage first. Missing parser/key/source/manifest coverage is INCONCLUSIVE, not proof of absence.
For multi-source findings preserve source_path/source_hash/parser/version/record native id so every narrative finding can be traced back to a concrete record.
Count distinct forensic entities/events after exclusions and semantic deduplication; never substitute a Section B raw artifact total for an objective-specific count.
